messages:
incident-bot: New incident INC-2026-042 created (severity: P2) — customer invoice vs dashboard delta reported for ACME.
maria: Fyi — ACME case 5582. They were billed 1,210,452 tokens for 2026-03-14 to 2026-03-15 but the dashboard shows ~898,311 tokens. Customer asks for explanation and credits. Escalating to eng + billing :wave:.
alex: Thanks. Can you paste a couple of request_ids and timestamps, and the ledger_id? Need to trace through ingestion.
maria: Provided in case file: req_8a1f (2026-03-14T02:12:03Z), req_8a2b (2026-03-14T02:13:41Z), req_9c3d (2026-03-14T03:05:22Z). Ledger: ledger_acme_202603.
jonah: Quick summary from infra side — we had a transient worker OOM on eventstore ingestion around 2026-03-14 02:00-04:30 UTC. Compaction paused, resulting in ~120k events backlog on meter-events topic. Offsets that look suspicious: 1245000..1259200. Consumer lag peaked ~120k.
alex: That aligns. If ingestion stalled, the metering pipeline may have dropped or retried some events. We need to replay the missing offset range into the metering service and then run reconciliation to compute token deltas.
sam: From billing: need an estimated delta in tokens and a proposed provisional credit. We can't issue any adjustments without eng reconciliation numbers.
tina: I can run an initial reconciliation query against the raw events store to get gross token total for ACME in the window. Suggest: run aggregator query to sum tokens by request_id and customer.
jonah: Query I ran (clickhouse-ish):
```
select customer_id, sum(tokens) as total_tokens
from meter_events_raw
where customer_id = 'acme' and event_time >= '2026-03-14 00:00:00' and event_time < '2026-03-16 00:00:00'
group by customer_id;
```
jonah: That returned 1,210,879 tokens from raw events (pre-ingestion). Dashboard shows 898,311 post-processed tokens. Rough delta ~312,568 tokens.
maria: Customer reported billed 1,210,452, close to raw. So it looks like metering processor only saw 898k; billing used raw/ledger which has full count — explains discrepancy.
alex: OK — plan: 1) run a replay of offsets 1245000..1259200 to meter-processor with dedupe/idempotency enabled; 2) run final reconciliation job to compute final ledger vs processed delta; 3) if results match raw, billing will adjust invoice/credits.
alex: Replay command (dry-run first):
```
replay_tool --topic meter-events --from-offset 1245000 --to-offset 1259200 --consumer-group metering-processor-replay --dry-run
```
alex: If dry-run looks good, run with --apply --dedupe-mode=on --idempotency-key=inc-2026-042. Note: previous run failed on duplicate keys — see error below.
replay-bot: replay attempt at 2026-03-14T13:22:11Z failed: duplicate key violation (metering_events_pkey).
alex: Past failure context: when two parallel replays ran we hit unique constraint. Use dedupe-mode and idempotency key to avoid reapplying the same logical event. Also ensure metering-processor is in read-only mode for ledger updates during replay or use dry-run to capture deltas first.
maria: I kicked off a dry-run at 2026-03-15T14:00Z per alex's command. Dry-run output (snippet):
```
DRY RUN: events scanned: 120134
potential new tokens: 312,568
potential duplicates detected: 3 (ids: req_7f6e, req_8a2b, req_9c3d)
```
maria: Customer sample req_8a2b is flagged duplicate in dry-run. That matches their sample.
jonah: For duplicates we have two choices: a) run dedupe pre-step to mark already-applied event ids and skip them, or b) run replay with dedupe-mode to let processor ignore duplicates. Dedupe-mode is preferable.
alex: When you switch to --apply with dedupe-mode, watch the metering-processor logs. If you see unique constraint still failing, STOP and we will run the SQL dedupe patch.
replay-bot: APPLY replay started at 2026-03-15T15:10:02Z with idempotency key inc-2026-042.
replay-bot: ERROR at 2026-03-15T15:12:37Z: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "metering_events_pkey" on insert.
alex: Ugh. Looks like dedupe-mode missed a race. Jonah — can you run the safe SQL backstop to remove exact duplicates before second attempt?
jonah: Running patch:
```
with duplicates as (
  select request_id, count(*) cnt
  from meter_events
  where customer_id='acme' and event_time >= '2026-03-14' and event_time < '2026-03-16'
  group by request_id
  having cnt > 1
)
delete from meter_events
where (customer_id='acme' and event_time >= '2026-03-14' and event_time < '2026-03-16')
and request_id in (select request_id from duplicates)
and ctid not in (
  select min(ctid) from meter_events group by request_id
);
```
jonah: Patch completed at 2026-03-15T16:05Z. Removed 3 duplicate rows.
alex: Re-run replay with --apply --dedupe-mode=on and idempotency key. Monitor for any unique constraint errors.
replay-bot: APPLY replay started at 2026-03-15T16:20:01Z. Completed at 2026-03-15T16:41:22Z. Events applied: 120131. Tokens added to ledger for acme: 312,568.
jonah: Post-replay reconciliation query:
```
select sum(tokens) from meter_events where customer_id='acme' and event_time >= '2026-03-14' and event_time < '2026-03-16';
-- result: 1,210,879
select ledger_balance from billing_ledger where ledger_id='ledger_acme_202603';
-- result: 1,210,452 (minor rounding/truncation difference ~427 tokens)
```
sam: From billing: we see ledger 1,210,452 vs processed 1,210,879. Difference = 427 tokens (likely rounding or ingestion timing). The customer's invoice matched ledger. Given the customer thought dashboard was ground truth, provisional credit approved for 312,141 tokens (difference between billed and dashboard). We'll issue provisional credit while we tidy up small 427-token discrepancy.
maria: I'll message the customer with the plan: provisional credit for 312,141 tokens now, final adjustment after we resolve the 427-token mismatch (should be small).
alex: Action items:
- jonah: run duplicate cleanup (done) and monitor pipeline (owner).
- alex: supervise final replay and reconciliation (done).
- sam: prepare provisional credit note and draft invoice adjustment (owner).
- maria: inform customer and set expectation for final confirmation in 48 hours.
maria: Sending message to customer now. Draft: "We identified an ingestion lag on 2026-03-14 that caused your dashboard to show fewer tokens than were billed. We have applied a provisional credit of 312,141 tokens while we complete the final reconciliation. We expect to confirm final numbers within 48 hours." :white_check_mark:
sam: I'll create an invoice credit record and notify finance.
alex: Recommend post-incident: add an automated check that compares ledger vs processed totals hourly and alerts when delta > 1% for >1 hour.
jonah: Agree. I'll add a runbook step to hold replays until dedupe marker table is in sync to avoid duplicate constraint errors.
maria: Closing loop: customer notified, provisional credit queued, replay and reconciliation complete. Will reopen if any further discrepancies. :lock_with_ink_pen:
summary: ACME invoice vs dashboard delta traced to eventstore ingestion lag (worker OOM) causing 120k events backlog. Replayed offsets 1245000..1259200 with dedupe + idempotency, removed duplicates via SQL backstop, applied 312,568 tokens to ledger; provisional credit of 312,141 tokens issued pending final 427-token reconciliation. Action items assigned to infra/eng/billing.
